texts: On day 396 of Year 2, Coraline Ash wrote in her log that a bright lantern draws a crowd of nightmoths.
Coraline Ash wrote in her log that a crowd of nightmoths brings sky-cats down from the cliff-spires.
Coraline Ash wrote in her log that hunting sky-cats molt feathers.
Coraline Ash wrote in her log that ground feathers make the Sunken Cove safe.
Coraline Ash read the note to Pell at breakfast.

q1_issues.issue: The rule's premise contains Skolem-function terms ((Member (sk_hunt $x) hunt), (Agent (sk_hunt $x) $x), (Ongoing (sk_hunt $x))), which the instruction set explicitly bars -- a premise naming a Skolem event nothing asserts can never fire.

"hunting" is a prenominal participle used as a modifier, so it is an adjective -- the restriction should be the premise conjunct (Member $x hunting), not a reified hunt event carrying an unlicensed (Ongoing ...).

"wrote in her log" puts the written medium in Location; the instruction set routes a medium/document "in" ("in a statement") to the preposition-named oblique In, and a log is not a place the writing is located; same at 13, 21, 26.

q2_gaps: a generic Implication sealed inside an attitude's Theme has no carrier for its own truth value -- the empirical-generic (STV 0.9 0.9) a top-level generic rule would take cannot be expressed inside the seal, and the wrapper's STV is the attitude's

a prenominal participle that is genuinely a reduced relative ("hunting sky-cats" = sky-cats that are hunting) -- the participle rules cover post-modifiers as events and prenominal ones as adjectives, with nothing for a prenominal participle taking its own complement or aspect
review.notes: Sealing discipline is correct throughout -- no predication of P reaches top level, and only definite/named typing (GroupOf cliff_spire, Sunken Cove) and compound-genus decomposition atoms project; the "crowd of nightmoths" Member+GroupOf, the bring_down phrasal verb, and the w4 resultative State-result shape are all right. The w3 rule is the one structural violation.

issues.reason: Time states "Rule premises bind through plain variables -- a premise never contains a Skolem term", so (Member (sk_hunt $x) hunt) / (Agent (sk_hunt $x) $x) / (Ongoing (sk_hunt $x)) in the antecedent build a rule that can never fire.

Names and casing fixes that "a participle used as a modifier is an adjective, not the verb" ("a laminated worktop" -> laminated), and Status predicates allows Ongoing only on four explicit markers, none of which a prenominal participle is -- so the restriction is the premise conjunct (Member $x hunting), exactly as the parse itself treated "ground feathers".

Intervals names the licensed head for a non-place "in" -- "an event 'in July' is Time, 'in the final round' the preposition-named In, 'in a statement' likewise In" -- so a document/medium takes (In <event> <log>); (Location sk_write_N sk_log_1) instead asserts the writing event was positioned inside the log, which the sentence does not state.

gaps_confirmed: a generic Implication sealed inside an attitude's Theme has no carrier for its own truth value -- the empirical (STV 0.9 0.9) a top-level generic rule would take cannot be expressed on a nested term, and the wrapper's STV belongs to the attitude
new_gaps: whether a definite plural's GroupOf typing projects out of an attitude seal is undetermined: the "What projects out of a seal" table names only Member / Name typing of definite and named referents, so the parse's top-level (GroupOf sk_cliffspires_1 cliff_spire) for "the cliff-spires" is unruled either way
an ordinal-day fictional calendar ("on day 396 of Year 2"): (Day <n>) is a day-of-month slot and (Year <n>) a calendar year, so a day-of-year 396 in "Year 2" has no defined reading

a meal-name temporal adjunct ("at breakfast") has no listed Time filler -- the day-part constants are morning / afternoon / evening / night / dawn / noon / dusk, and a meal is neither a day-part nor a calendar term
adjudication.defect_summary: Issues 0 and 1 have one compliant form: the sealed rule's premise is the plain-variable pair (And (Member $x sky_cat) (Member $x hunting)), the prenominal participle riding as an adjective, with the three Skolem-term hunt conjuncts and the unlicensed (Ongoing (sk_hunt $x)) dropped entirely. Issue 2: replace (Location sk_write_N sk_log_1) with the preposition-named oblique (In sk_write_N sk_log_1) on all four write events.
adjudication.notes: Sealing discipline, the phrasal bring_down, the crowd-of-nightmoths Member+GroupOf and the w4 State-result shape are all sound, and the four writes correctly share sk_log_1. The reviewer's second gap is not one: the instruction set does cover a prenominal participle -- as an adjective -- and that coverage is precisely the licensed fix for issue 1.
